## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

As observed in doctrinal studies of Pali Buddhism, whereas earlier discourses across the Nikāyas do not furnish a rigid formal specification for *vipassanā*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* introduces its foundational technical definition: insight is understood essentially in the sense of contemplation as impermanent (*aniccato anupassanā*) and contemplation as painful (*dukkhato anupassanā*) [Wen].

 DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these connections through machine-computed text reuse, identifying 1,087 matching passages across 55 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlaps occur with the *Chakkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 6), where Ps 3.9 §4.1–6.1 closely corresponds to AN 6.98–99, as well as with other Aṅguttara books (AN 10, AN 5, AN 7) and Mnd 2 (§11.2 matching Mnd §105.2–105.3) [DharmaNexus]. Extensive verbatim reuse is also detected in later exegetical literature, notably the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Visuddhimagga*, and its *Mahāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies automated cross-language alignments with Chinese Āgamas (such as the *Saṃyuktāgama*, T99, and the *Madhyamāgama*, T26) and Tibetan canonical translations, including the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D3790-3) and the *Ārya-niṣṭhāgata-bhagavajjñānavaipulya-sūtra* (D0099) [DharmaNexus].
